correctness.rationale: Both the frozen coloring arguments and the narrowed theorem are mathematically correct. In K_{3,n} with n>=3, the shores have disjoint vertex palettes. With three colors, if both shores are monochromatic then all edges receive the remaining color and contain a four-cycle. Otherwise one shore uses two colors, of which one repeats, and the other uses one color; edges from two equally colored vertices to two vertices of the other shore are forced to the same third color, again a four-cycle. Fewer than three colors are impossible at an incident edge and its endpoints. With four colors, the opposite shore is colored 4, the smaller shore gets 1,2,3, and the respective full incident stars get 2,3,1. Every nonempty edge class is one star and every edge avoids both endpoint colors. For n>=5, two forests on n+3 vertices can cover at most 2(n+2)<3n edges, so a four-color construction cannot use disjoint edge and vertex palettes. The repaired result and verification notes state these scopes accurately.
residual_risks: The frozen source described the positive three-color checks as exhaustively testing every vertex assignment, but verify.py stops at the first witness. This is sufficient for the finite decision and does not affect the infinite proof; the repaired notes specify the stopping rule. The frozen verifier was not executed.

evidence: Theorem 6 establishes exact four for K_{3,3}-e. Theorem 1 establishes a three-color upper bound for any acyclic three-vertex-coloring. The 2016 planar-bipartite construction uses disjoint edge and vertex palettes; that method cannot give four colors on K_{3,n} when n>=5 by the elementary forest capacity bound.

originality.rationale: PASS for the repaired claim only. The frozen finding's headline three-color threshold fails originality: the actual 2016 Theorem 6 sharpness example K_{3,3}-e forces failure for all m,n>=3 by subgraph inheritance, while Theorem 1 covers K_{2,n} from an acyclic three-coloring and stars are immediate. The narrowed exact value four for K_{3,n} retains the original nonplanar upper-bound contribution and explicitly credits prior support for the lower bound. The checked general acyclic-coloring theorem gives five from four acyclic vertex colors; the four-color upper bounds in the checked papers are for planar graphs. They do not give the uniform four-color upper bound for the nonplanar family.
residual_risks: The 2011 paper remains a plausible source of an earlier related construction, but its full text was not accessible. The bounded search does not certify priority for the surviving formula.

value.rationale: The repaired theorem computes the sharp invariant on the first complete-bipartite shore size excluded by the old three-color criterion. This is a natural nonplanar test family for the same four-color invariant studied in the planar literature. For n>=5, simply putting the vertex and edge colors in disjoint palettes cannot attain four; the explicit rotation of the three star colors solves that obstruction for every n. Thus the exact family value is useful independently of the already implied three-color threshold.
residual_risks: No exact formula is claimed for smaller shore size at least four, nor is it asserted that every proper four-vertex-coloring of K_{3,n} extends.
